function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time weather information. You might check a reliable weather website or app (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or your local meteorological service) for the current temperature in Moscow.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What weather is now in Moscow, in Celsius?" They want current temperature in Moscow in Celsius. We need to provide the answer. There's no tool for weather. So we just respond with the current temperature. But we don't have real-time data. We can approximate or say we can't fetch live data. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. We can say we cannot provide real-time data. Or we could use a placeholder. The best approach: explain that I can't fetch real-time data.
